title: The Future: will & going to
subtitle: Plans, predictions, promises and quick decisions

beats.caption: Tomorrow, I'm <v>going to follow</v> the map!
Don't worry, Grandma. I <v>will be</v> careful.

say: I'm going to follow the map. I will be careful. Two different ways to talk about the future, in two sentences.
Today you'll learn when to use will, when to use going to, and the mistakes to avoid.

data.heading: will or going to?
rows: I'm going to visit Grandma on Friday.
The phone's ringing. I'll answer it!
going to = I can see it coming
Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
I think you'll love this film.

say: Here's the big picture.
Going to is for plans you made before: I'm going to visit Grandma on Friday.
Will is for decisions you make at the moment of speaking: the phone's ringing. I'll answer it!
Going to is also for predictions with evidence, things you can see coming: look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
And will is for opinions about the future: I think you'll love this film.

data.heading: Form: am / is / are + going to + base verb

say: Going to has three parts: am, is or are, then going to, then the base verb.
I'm going to travel.
She's going to travel.
They're going to travel.
For the negative, add not: she isn't going to travel. I'm not going to travel.
The sun is setting. Mia and Whiskers are going to walk home before it gets dark.
beats.caption: They<v>'re going to walk</v> home before dark.

say: Will is even easier. It's the same for every subject, and it's followed by the base verb.
We'll help you.
It'll be fine. No s, no ing.
The negative is won't: I won't tell anyone.
And for questions, start with will: will you come?

data.heading: More uses of will
examples: That bag looks heavy. I'll <v>carry</v> it.

say: Will has some other jobs, too.
Promises: I will always remember you.
Offers: that bag looks heavy. I'll carry it.
Requests: will you open the window, please?
And quick decisions, like in a restaurant: I'll have the chicken, please.
In everyday speaking, we usually say the short form: I'll, you'll, she'll.

beats.caption: Don't worry, Grandma. I <v>will be</v> careful.

data.heading: Saying it naturally
data.tip: gonna: speaking only, never in writing

say: How do native speakers really say these?
Will becomes a short l sound: I'll, you'll, she'll, we'll.
Going to often sounds like gonna: I'm gonna, it's gonna, we're gonna. You can say it, but don't write it in exams.
And be careful with won't and want. Won't has an o sound. Want has an a sound. I won't go. I want to go.
Gonna is for speaking only. In writing, always use going to.
Look at the river! The stones are wet. Mia is going to slip! Whiskers, I'll help you!
beats.caption: Careful! She<v>'s going to slip</v>!

data.heading: Questions and short answers
data.rule: Are you going to ...? / Will you ...?
pairs: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
Yes, I will. / No, I won't.

say: Questions. With going to, move am, is or are to the front.
Are you going to study tonight? Yes, I am. Or, no, I'm not.
Is it going to rain? Yes, it is.
With will, start with will: will you help me? Yes, I will. Or, no, I won't.
What are you going to do? I'm going to call Grandma.
These words tell us we're talking about the future.
Tomorrow. Tonight. Next week. Next year.
Soon. In two days. That means two days from now.
And one day, which means some time in the future: one day, I'll be a pilot.

data.heading: Common mistakes (Arabic speakers)
rows: Tomorrow I go to the doctor.
Tomorrow I'm going to the doctor.
I will call you when I will arrive.
I'll call you when I arrive.

say: Let's fix the common mistakes.
I will to go tomorrow. No to after will: I will go tomorrow.
She wills come. Will never takes s: she will come.
I going to study. Don't forget am: I'm going to study.
Tomorrow I go to the doctor. For a plan, say: tomorrow I'm going to the doctor, or I'm going to go to the doctor.
I will call you when I will arrive. After when, use the present: I'll call you when I arrive.

data.heading: Repeat after me
lines: I'm going to visit my grandma.

repeat.text: I'm going to visit my grandma.

say: Now you. Listen, then say it out loud.

data.heading: The big day
data.sub: Listen for will and going to

say: One more story. Listen for will, and going to.
Mia shows Grandma the map. Grandma smiles. I think it will be a great adventure, she says. But you're going to need a warm jacket.
beats.caption: You<v>'re going to need</v> a warm jacket.
Tomorrow, I'm <v>going to follow</v> the map!

say: The next morning, Mia walks to the hills with a big smile. It's going to be a beautiful day, she thinks. And it will be.
beats.caption: It<v>'s going to be</v> a beautiful day.

data.heading: Your turn!
data.sub: Pause the video if you need more time

say: Quiz time. Five questions, five seconds each.

data.q: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.

beats.say_answer: Is going to. We can see the evidence: the clouds.

data.q: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it!

beats.say_answer: Visit. After will, the base verb.
Am. I am going to study tonight.

data.q: I'll call you when I ___ home.

beats.say_answer: Get. After when, use the present simple.

data.heading: Remember
items: going to: plans + predictions you can see
will: quick decisions, promises, offers, opinions
am / is / are + going to + base verb
will + base verb (no to, no s)
when / after + present: when I arrive

say: Let's remember. Going to is for plans and for predictions you can see. Will is for quick decisions, promises, offers and opinions.
Going to needs am, is or are. Will is followed by the base verb, with no to and no s. And won't means will not.
Finally, after when, use the present: I'll call you when I arrive.
